teaching.hint: How can one position represent the objective of whichever player is about to move?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: The current mover’s best score difference on an interval subtracts the next mover’s best difference after either endpoint choice.
solution_outline.approach: Use interval dynamic programming, with range sums for the immediate reward. For each interval, compare removing its left or right end and subtract the continuation value of the remaining interval.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: A state for interval [i,j] is the maximum current-mover score minus opponent score from that position. A one-stone interval has value zero.
solution_outline.correctness: Every legal first move is one of the two endpoints. The immediate remaining sum is gained by the mover; the opponent’s optimal future difference must be subtracted. Taking the better option gives the optimal differential by induction on interval length.
solution_outline.complexity: O(n²) time and O(n²) space with constant-time range sums.
solution_outline.pitfall: Adding the continuation value instead of subtracting it assumes both players share the same objective.

common_wrong_turns: Score the removed stone rather than the remaining stones
Treat Bob as maximizing Alice’s advantage
source_fidelity_notes: Condensed the long move-by-move example; explicitly retained last-removal zero reward.
